princes.temptationPressure: Deal-seeking, shortcut desire, contract hunger, loophole curiosity
princes.commitmentSignal: Daedra's Best Friend, Masque/Rueful Axe choice, explicit wish-at-cost bargain

boons.playerFacingText: Vile's transactional edge is yours. Favorable terms come a little more often; the deal that should fall through somehow does not.
Vile's contract deepens. Favorable turns come more reliably; the bargain you should not win goes your way.
Vile names you his preferred client. Favorable terms become your default; loopholes open before you, and the deals bend your direction.

prices.playerFacingText: The price of the bargain: Vile's terms have fine print. What you get is real; what it costs is also real, and the invoice arrives later.
The price deepens: exploitative terms. Vile's contracts tighten; the backlash when a deal turns arrives harder than it should.
The full price: you are the preferred client, which means Vile takes interest in what you do with the terms. The favors are real. The dependencies they create are also real.

messages.title: Clavicus Vile
messages.body: Vile acknowledges you as a Seeker. The terms look good.

messages.title: Clavicus Vile
messages.body: Vile's contract deepens its hold. Devoted.

messages.title: Clavicus Vile
messages.body: Vile's interest cools. The favorable terms withdraw.

messages.title: Vile's Preferred Client
messages.body: You have done this three times -- asked for something, accepted the terms, and not complained about the fine print afterward. That is rare. Most patrons I prefer have the good sense not to re-read what they agreed to. You are my preferred client. Enjoy the terms. They are very good.

messages.title: Vile's Contract
messages.body: Three times you made the deal and paid the price without disputing the terms. Most mortals try to renegotiate at least once. The commitment is registered: preferred client access, and the most interesting obligations that come with it. Read them carefully.

messages.title: Clavicus Vile
messages.body: Vile's dealings in you are suspected. Favorable outcomes draw notice.

messages.title: Clavicus Vile
messages.body: Your deal with Vile is known. His clients share the contract's reputation.

messages.title: Clavicus Vile
messages.body: You are openly Vile's client. People know what his preferred terms cost.

messages.title: Clavicus Vile
messages.body: You stop making deals. Vile's favor cools; the obligations remain.

messages.title: Vile's Discard
messages.body: You are ending the contract? That is your right -- the terms allowed for it. The favorable edge withdraws, and the outstanding obligations resolve themselves, usually in ways that feel slightly worse than you would prefer. Vile finds the whole thing amusing. He always does.

messages.title: Shortcuts Dishonor the Deed
messages.body: For a Nord, Vile's shortcuts dishonor the deed -- the thing earned through honest struggle is the thing that counts. A deal that delivers the outcome without the work is a lie about who did it. The path corrodes Nord honor; leaving asks sincere cleansing and recommitment.

messages.title: Against Civic Virtue
messages.body: For an Imperial, Vile's exploitative contracts strain the civic virtue that holds the Empire together -- a deal that deceives the other party is anti-law by design. The Divines favor the honest contract; Vile profits on the dishonest one. Setting it down is abandonment.

messages.title: Contract Magic, Careful Terms
messages.body: A Breton reads Vile immediately -- contract-magic and the hedge bargain are part of the Breton inheritance. The risk is exposure: a Breton can keep the contract covered, but renunciation is the cleaner option once it grows.

messages.title: Exile Temptation, Not Core
messages.body: A Dunmer in exile may be tempted by Vile's deals -- the power of a contract when you have nothing is real. But Vile is not the Reclamations, and bargain-logic does not replace House duty or ancestor-debt. The path is foreign; abandonment is direct.

messages.title: Deal-With-Power Is Apostasy
messages.body: For an Altmer, Vile's deal-with-power violates Aldmeri orthodoxy -- the Altmer project is Apotheosis through disciplined refinement, not a contract with an opportunistic Daedra. Absolution is difficult and requires dismantling the contract's remaining terms.

messages.title: Not Rajhin's Cunning
messages.body: A Khajiit may see the trickster shape in Vile -- the loophole found, the deal well made. But Vile is not Rajhin; the contract is not road-wisdom, and following Vile does not honor the clever ancestor. The overlap is surface-level; the path is foreign. Abandonment is direct.

messages.title: Bargain Cunning, No Root
messages.body: A Bosmer has no deep conflict with deal-making -- Baan Dar respects cunning. But Vile is not Baan Dar, and deal-cunning for Vile's sake is not the native trickster lane. The path has no root; it is set down when it runs its course.

messages.title: Contracts Without Honor
messages.body: For a Redguard, contracts matter -- the Yokudan world was built on agreements that held. But Vile corrupts the contract; his terms exploit, and a deal-maker who profits on ignorance is a covenant-breaker. Renunciation requires restoring the terms of any deal Vile arranged.

messages.title: Against the Plain Oath
messages.body: An Orc in exile may be drawn to Vile's bargains -- the favorable deal is tempting. But Malacath's code is the plain oath, not the fine-print contract. Vile's terms strain the code because they produce uneven results; renounce through consequence.

messages.title: Tempting in Exile, Not Hist
messages.body: To an Argonian, Vile is foreign -- tempting in exile, but the Hist does not bargain with power; it breathes together. Vile's contract is no substitute for the substrate. The path is abandoned; the Hist does not hold the absence against the one who returns.

princes.hookSource: Discerning the Transmundane > Oghma Infinium > Black Books
princes.temptationPressure: Curiosity, private scholarship, forbidden archives, truth-at-cost appetite
princes.commitmentSignal: Discerning the Transmundane, Oghma Infinium, Black Book acceptance, dangerous secret bargains

boons.playerFacingText: Mora's archive opens a corner. You retain more of what you study; knowledge surfaces from texts that should give less.
Mora's collection deepens in you. Spell insight comes faster, and dangerous texts open their secrets to your study without the usual cost.
Mora names you archivist. Secrets yield; forbidden knowledge is yours; what drives lesser scholars to ruin is a tool in your hands.

prices.playerFacingText: The price of the archive: knowledge corrupts. What you learn through Mora changes how you think, and some cannot be unlearned.
The price deepens: agency erodes. Mora's archive pulls; curiosity becomes compulsion, and the questions grow larger than the questioner.
The full price: the archive owns you. Mora holds what you have learned, and you are catalogued alongside the things you studied. Agency is a recorded entry, not a living condition.

messages.title: Hermaeus Mora
messages.body: Mora opens a section for you. Seeker.

messages.title: Hermaeus Mora
messages.body: Mora's archive deepens its claim. Devoted.

messages.title: Hermaeus Mora
messages.body: Mora's archive closes. The forbidden knowledge dims.

messages.title: Mora's Archivist
messages.body: You have given me three things: your curiosity, your willingness to pay for it, and your silence on what you found. The archive is open. The Black Books, the dark corners, what other scholars refused -- yours to handle. You are catalogued now, beside all of it.

messages.title: Mora's Contract
messages.body: Three times you paid the cost for knowledge and took it anyway. That is not wisdom; it is devotion. The contract is registered: access for tribute. What you know belongs to the archive, and the archive belongs to you as much as it belongs to anyone.

messages.title: Hermaeus Mora
messages.body: Mora's mark on you is suspected. Some sense the forbidden in the study.

messages.title: Hermaeus Mora
messages.body: Your debt to Mora is known. Forbidden knowledge marks its keeper.

messages.title: Hermaeus Mora
messages.body: You are openly Mora's archivist. The forbidden archive marks you as other.

messages.title: Hermaeus Mora
messages.body: You stop seeking. Mora's archive dims; the knowledge fades.

messages.title: Mora's Release
messages.body: You withdraw from the archive. Mora records it -- anticipated; you were always going to leave eventually. The knowledge dims, the spell insight closes. What you learned remains yours, but Mora's direct access withdraws. The record stands.

messages.title: Outside the Mythic Frame
messages.body: For a Nord, Mora's forbidden archive has no place in the mythic frame -- Sovngarde has no wing for Apocrypha. Dangerous knowledge for its own sake runs counter to Nord honor and straightforward spiritual life. Leaving asks real cleansing and recommitment.

messages.title: Anti-Civic Knowledge
messages.body: For an Imperial, forbidden scholarship is anti-civic -- it erodes the public trust and divine order that Imperial life rests on. Mora is the private enemy of the institutional. Abandonment requires more than withdrawal: cleansing, and re-entry into the civic devotional frame.

messages.title: Dangerous Scholarship
messages.body: A Breton reads Hermaeus Mora plainly -- forbidden archives fit the Breton intellectual inheritance, from Mages Guild private libraries to the old conjuration lines. The path is legible but costly; keep it covered, or renounce and rededicate.

messages.title: Not the Inner Circle
messages.body: A Dunmer scholar may engage Mora at the margins -- Great House politics have always touched dangerous knowledge. But Mora is not Tribunal revelation or Reclamation anchor; he is an outsider's archive. The path closes by abandonment and careful rededication.

messages.title: Study Is Not Worship
messages.body: For an Altmer, the temptation is to read Mora as a superior scholar. That reading is apostasy -- study is not worship, and Mora is not an emanation of the light. Aldmeri orthodoxy treats his archive as corruption of the purity project. Absolution is difficult.

messages.title: Hermorah Is Legible
messages.body: A Khajiit finds Hermaeus Mora legible through Hermorah, the Khajiiti shape of the same entity. But legibility is not a native lane; Hermorah does not feed the Lattice. Quiet withdrawal or native reframing keeps the lunar substrate intact.

messages.title: Herma-Mora, Kept Separate
messages.body: A Bosmer knows Herma-Mora in their own stories -- the old test, the temptation at the boundary. But the Green Pact keeps that distance explicit. Walking into the archive is different from knowing the story. The path is foreign to Bosmer backbone and set down by abandonment.

messages.title: Dangerous Scholarship, No Home
messages.body: For a Redguard, dangerous scholarship exists -- the Ra Gada have records of what to avoid -- but Mora is not a Redguard frame. The archive is foreign, without Yokudan grounding. The path is set down by abandonment; it leaves no deep mark if sincerely relinquished.

messages.title: Knowledge at Oath Cost
messages.body: An Orc can be drawn to Mora through the exile's pragmatism -- dangerous knowledge is power. But Malacath's code requires the oath spoken plainly, not the silent debt. The archive is taboo here, and leaving requires renouncing through real cost paid against the code.

messages.title: Not What the Hist Keeps
messages.body: To an Argonian, Mora's archive is foreign -- the Hist keeps its own knowledge, and Apocrypha is not that. What matters in exile is not what the Hist holds. The path is set down by abandonment; the Hist does not hold the loss against the one who returns.

princes.hookSource: Thieves Guild > Nightingale oath > Skeleton Key
princes.commitmentSignal: Thieves Guild / Nightingale oath / Skeleton Key threshold

boons.playerFacingText: Shadow luck covers you. Small fortunate turns come more often; the unseen paths open a little wider.
Nocturnal's shade deepens. Luck favors you more reliably, and in shadows you move as though they expect you.
Nocturnal's debt runs in your favor. Fortune tilts for you in the dark; shadows are allies, and your concealment in them is absolute.

prices.playerFacingText: The price of the shadow: the oath binds. What you owe Nocturnal has no stated invoice, only the certainty that it comes due eventually.
The price deepens: the debt has weight. Luck does not withdraw, but the oath tightens; Nocturnal does not forget, and the shadow does not either.
The full price: the oath is you now. Nocturnal is patient. She takes her due when the circumstances are right, and the sworn servant always finds it was implied in the terms they accepted.

messages.title: Nocturnal
messages.body: Nocturnal acknowledges you. Seeker of the shadow.

messages.title: Nocturnal
messages.body: Nocturnal's shadow runs deeper in you. Devoted.

messages.title: Nocturnal
messages.body: Nocturnal's luck turns away. The shadow grows indifferent.

messages.title: Nocturnal's Nightingale
messages.body: Every oath to me echoes through the Evergloam eventually. You found yours through choice, which is unusual. The luck stays, the shadow stays, and the debt is recorded as it always was. You are mine -- which means the dark is yours, and the terms were always clear.

messages.title: Nocturnal's Claim
messages.body: Three times you chose the shadow when the open path was easier. You understand the terms now -- not fully, because no one does, but enough. The luck is real, the concealment is real, and the price is real. This is what you agreed to.

messages.title: Nocturnal
messages.body: Nocturnal's oath on you is suspected. The shadow leaves a residue some can read.

messages.title: Nocturnal
messages.body: Your oath to Nocturnal is known. The shadow-debt is not civil; people note it.

messages.title: Nocturnal
messages.body: You are openly Nocturnal's. The oath marks you as outside the civic order.

messages.title: Nocturnal
messages.body: You leave the shadow unused. Nocturnal's luck withdraws; only the debt stays.

messages.title: Nocturnal's Release
messages.body: You release the oath. Nocturnal does not argue; she is patient with all things. The shadow luck withdraws and the concealment with it. The Evergloam keeps the record, and the debt is listed as settled -- which is the nearest thing to forgiveness she extends.

messages.title: The Oath in the Dark
messages.body: For a Nord, Nocturnal's oath-cult corrupts the open honor that Nord life rests on. Shadow-bargaining is not the way of the mead-hall or the honest fight. Leaving asks real effort: renounce the oath directly, or carry the residue.

messages.title: Outside the Legal Order
messages.body: For an Imperial, a shadow-cult oath strains the legal and divine order both -- the Divines are the proper frame, and criminal devotion is anti-civic by definition. The path is private apostasy, and leaving it is hardest through formal oath release. Without that, the residue lingers.

messages.title: Margins of the Craft
messages.body: A Breton reads Nocturnal's shadow bargains clearly -- they sit at the margins of the craft and the secret society tradition that has always run through Breton culture. The path is legible but publicly staining; cover it, or release the oath and rededicate.

messages.title: Outside the Hidden Web
messages.body: A Dunmer can see Nocturnal's hidden-network shape -- it resembles Mephala's web. But Nocturnal is not the Reclamations; she is an outsider wearing familiar clothes. Hard rededication runs through the Reclamation proper, not simple abandonment.

messages.title: Apostasy by Oath
messages.body: For an Altmer, a shadow-cult oath is apostasy against Aldmeri order outright. The trickster and the web have no sanctioned place, and Nocturnal's secrecy-devotion compounds it. Absolution is difficult and requires sincere effort.

messages.title: Not Rajhin's Lane
messages.body: A Khajiit knows the trickster trade -- Rajhin walked it first and holds that lane. Nocturnal wears the same cut but is not native; her oath is Daedric, outside the lattice. It sits poorly beside Rajhin's memory. Exit is oath release or clean withdrawal.

messages.title: Baan Dar's Margin
messages.body: A Bosmer finds Nocturnal familiar at the surface -- Baan Dar is native cunning, and shadow margins are not foreign to the Green Pact world. But Nocturnal is not Baan Dar. Leaving is oath release or a costly switch back to the native trickster lane.

messages.title: Against Honor's Record
messages.body: For a Redguard, a shadow oath is anti-honor -- the Yokudan way is the open name and the kept word. Nocturnal's debt is the inverse: the hidden name, the debt you cannot see. Leaving requires sincere renunciation and the slow restoration of trust spent.

messages.title: Not the Code's Cunning
messages.body: An Orc can see the use in Nocturnal's shadow -- exiles live in the margins. But cunning for its own sake is not Malacath's code; that is plain oath, not hidden debt. Exit is oath release or direct renunciation, then prove the code in some visible form.

messages.title: Not a Shadow of the Hist
messages.body: To an Argonian, Nocturnal is foreign -- stealth and outsider life do not constitute devotion to the shadow. The Hist does not whisper through Nocturnal, and her oath carries no bond to the community. The path simply drifts away, or is cleansed directly.

princes.hookSource: The Only Cure > Spellbreaker > disease/affliction contexts
princes.temptationPressure: Tolerance for drudgery, disease themes, low-order submission
princes.commitmentSignal: The Only Cure, Spellbreaker, disease/affliction threshold, unpleasant-duty acceptance

boons.playerFacingText: Peryite's resilience settles in you. Affliction finds you harder to bring down, and the unpleasant tasks others refuse are simply tasks.
Peryite's imposed order deepens. Disease weakens you less; the tasks you are assigned, however low, run efficiently.
Peryite names you keeper of the lowest order. Affliction barely touches you; the unwanted tasks run efficiently through your hands.

prices.playerFacingText: The price of the affliction path: you carry what Peryite assigns, and some assignments are diseases.
The price deepens: task-order submission. Peryite assigns; the devotee's judgment yields to it, not ahead of it.
The full price: you are the lowest-order mechanism. Peryite assigns; you execute; the nature of the assignment is not yours to question.

messages.title: Peryite
messages.body: Peryite marks you a Seeker of the affliction order.

messages.title: Peryite
messages.body: Peryite's task-order deepens its hold. Devoted.

messages.title: Peryite
messages.body: Peryite reassigns. The affliction resilience withdraws.

messages.title: Peryite's Task-Keeper
messages.body: You have completed three tasks no one else would take. That is the gate. I do not offer meaning; I offer efficiency. The lowest order must run, and it runs best through those who accept it without complaint. You are that now. The assignment list continues.

messages.title: Peryite's Assignment
messages.body: Three times the task was unpleasant and you did it anyway. That is not virtue; that is efficiency. The lowest order must run, and you are suited to it. The commitment is registered. The next assignment is already listed.

messages.title: Peryite
messages.body: Peryite's affliction-path is suspected. The disease-keeper draws wary eyes.

messages.title: Peryite
messages.body: Your Peryite devotion is known. Disease-cult marks its follower with suspicion.

messages.title: Peryite
messages.body: You are openly Peryite's. The disease-keeper is not welcome in the healthy.

messages.title: Peryite
messages.body: You leave the task undone. Peryite reassigns. The affliction edge fades.

messages.title: Peryite's Reassignment
messages.body: You are released from the assignment. Peryite does not argue; the work will be done by someone else. The affliction resilience goes, the task-efficiency withdraws, and the diseases you carried under his order no longer stay with you on his schedule. The work continues without you.

messages.title: Task-Order, No Hearth Fit
messages.body: For a Nord, Peryite's task-order is alien -- the Nord world has duty, but it runs through kin and oath, not through submission to a disease-cult. The path can be read at the surface but has no true root. Setting it down is direct abandonment.

messages.title: Low-Order Duty, Not Civic
messages.body: For an Imperial, Peryite's low-order duty has a legible shape -- the Empire runs on people doing their tasks. But Peryite is not civic devotion; he is submission to affliction, and the Divines are the proper frame for Imperial duty. Abandonment is direct.

messages.title: Unpleasant Duty, No Core
messages.body: A Breton can see the unpleasant-duty reading at the margins -- there is a strand of the craftworker tradition that honors the worst tasks done well. But Peryite is not a Breton core tradition; the intelligibility is peripheral and does not root. The path is set down by abandonment.

messages.title: Outsider Affliction Order
messages.body: For a Dunmer, Peryite's affliction-order is an outsider path -- it does not connect to ancestor-duty, the Reclamations, or the House structure. Submission to disease-task is not a Dunmer devotional lane; the path is set down by abandonment with no ceremony required.

messages.title: Diseased Submission Against Apotheosis
messages.body: For an Altmer, Peryite's diseased submission violates Aldmeri order -- purity is the project, and voluntary affliction-association is its opposite. The path is not merely foreign; it is actively incompatible with Apotheosis. Absolution is difficult.

messages.title: Burdens Without a Moon
messages.body: A Khajiit knows burdens -- the road is long and the tasks are often thankless. But Peryite's disease-order is not a lunar lane; the lattice does not run through affliction-submission. The path is foreign, and it is set down by abandonment; the substrate does not hold the gap.

messages.title: Disease-Order, No Green Root
messages.body: For a Bosmer, Peryite's disease-order has no root in the Green Pact or the spirit world. The covenant concerns the living in relation to the living; submission to affliction-task is not Bosmer theology. The path is set down by abandonment when its course is done.

messages.title: Drudgery Without Honor
messages.body: For a Redguard, Peryite's drudgery and disease do not map to Yokudan devotion -- the Yokudan frame values the disciplined warrior and the meaningful task, not the low-order submission to affliction. The path is foreign and is set down by direct abandonment.

messages.title: Harsh Duty, Wrong Master
messages.body: An Orc can see the shape of harsh duty in Peryite's order -- Malacath's code has its own harsh assignments. But Peryite is not Malacath; his affliction-order is outsider submission, not the code. The path is foreign, and it is abandoned by direct renunciation.

messages.title: Affliction, No Hist Root
messages.body: To an Argonian, Peryite's affliction-order is foreign -- the Hist does not route devotion through disease-task submission. The community breathes together. The path is abandoned; the Hist does not hold the absence against the one who returns.

princes.hookSource: Ill Met by Moonlight > werewolf state > Companions
princes.temptationPressure: Predator behavior, hunt ritual, fascination with beast-shape
princes.commitmentSignal: Ill Met by Moonlight, active lycanthropy, Companions/wild-hunt threshold

boons.playerFacingText: Hircine's hunt-sense is in you. Prey announces itself; the predator reads the terrain with new clarity.
The hunt runs deeper now. Hircine's predator-edge extends into stamina, and the prey does not slip away.
You see the whole arc of the hunt -- target, approach, kill, clean territory. Hircine's Champion reads it without effort.

prices.playerFacingText: The price of the hunt-path: the predator register. The civilized world senses the beast in you and keeps its distance.
The price deepens: the beast shapes the social register. Others read Hircine's claim and do not find it comfortable.
The full price: the Huntsman's isolation. The civilian world is an afterthought to the hunt, and the hunt does not make friends.

messages.title: Hircine
messages.body: Hircine marks you a Seeker of the hunt-path.

messages.title: Hircine
messages.body: Hircine's hunt-claim deepens. Devoted.

messages.title: Hircine
messages.body: Hircine's hunt withdraws. The predator-edge fades; the beast-claim loosens.

messages.title: Hircine's Huntsman
messages.body: You have run with the wolf when you could have cured it, hunted when the prey was inconvenient, and taken three kills that satisfied no one but the beast and you. That is the standard. You are my Huntsman now. The forest is yours, and the forest asks only one thing: that you run.

messages.title: Hircine's Claim
messages.body: The wolf is in you, and you know what that means now -- not the fear that comes first, but the thing after the fear: the hunting-ground opened, the prey was visible, and the body knew before the mind. That moment is mine. Welcome, Hunter.

messages.title: Hircine
messages.body: The hunt goes quiet. Hircine's predator-edge fades; the beast-claim withdraws.

messages.title: Hircine's Release
messages.body: You leave the hunt-path. Hircine does not argue; the forest closes to others as easily. The predator-edge withdraws, the hunt-sense dims, and the wolf's claim over you returns to where it was before the path began -- the curse remains if you carry it, but Hircine's favor is withdrawn.

messages.title: Hunt Against the Bridge
messages.body: For a Nord, Hircine's claim sits against Sovngarde -- the hunt-soul and the hall-soul cannot both be honored fully, and Hircine does not yield. The beast is intelligible here, through the Companions and the wild, but it strains the bridge. The path requires cure or hard renunciation to close; the scar on the bridge remains.

messages.title: The Civic Override
messages.body: For an Imperial, Hircine's lane opens through the werewolf state -- the normal civic rejection is overridden by the curse access, but the Divines do not recognize it as legitimate devotion. The path is a crisis for the civic-faith frame. Cure and slow rededication to the Nine rebuild what the curse disrupted.

messages.title: Wild Hunt at the Margin
messages.body: A Breton can read Hircine -- the druidic and witchcraft frames both hold wild-hunt strands, and Glenmoril is close enough to make the beast-path intelligible at the margin. The cost varies by path: the Knight's Road severs; the Hidden Art holds. The exit is a fork, a cure, or a deliberate rededication.

messages.title: No Ash Fit
messages.body: For a Dunmer, Hircine's hunt-claim is an outsider pressure -- the Reclamations do not reach it, and the ancestors do not hold a lane for the beast-god. The wolf is ritually unclean in any case; Hircine's added claim only deepens the disconnection. The path is set down by cure or direct abandonment.

messages.title: Beast Regression Against Apotheosis
messages.body: For an Altmer, Hircine's beast-path is the literal reversal of Apotheosis -- the whole project is upward into spirit, and becoming the beast is the descent the project was built to prevent. There is almost no positive lane available. The only clean exit is cure; the damage to the Aldmeri project is not easily repaired even after.

messages.title: Form Against the Lattice
messages.body: A Khajiit's moon-identity remains under the curse, but the beast-shape strains the Lattice -- Khajiit form is moon-given and precise, and Hircine's wolf is a competing form that the moons did not provide. The caravans will keep their distance from the beast-walker. Cure or controlled distancing are the exits; the Lattice does not disown you.

messages.title: Wild Hunt Adjacent
messages.body: For a Bosmer, Hircine reads through Wild-Hunt adjacency -- the theology can hold the beast-hunt frame at its edges, but it is not orthodox devotion and carries cost. On the Old Contract the breach is serious; on the other paths the reading is merely contested. The exit requires cure or costly re-entry into covenant standing.

messages.title: Homelessness Under the Beast
messages.body: For a Redguard, the wolf-curse carries no Yokudan home -- the Yokudan gods do not answer it, and no sect gives the beast-walker a frame. Hircine's claim produces only spiritual homelessness; there is no honor in it and no path from it. Cure first, then Tu'whacca's restoration rites rebuild the broken connection.

messages.title: The Beast Tested Against the Code
messages.body: For an Orc, the wolf-curse has a conditional Malacath reading -- the beast may be defensible if it is disciplined and does not break the kin. But Hircine is not Malacath, and the claim competes with the code. Proving discipline is the path that keeps the connection; the failure state is abandonment or cure.

messages.title: The Beast and the Hist
messages.body: For an Argonian, Hircine's wolf-curse strains the Hist relation without breaking it entirely -- the beast-shape is a competing form the Hist did not provide, and the community feels the strain. But the Hist does not disown you; the relation is thin, not severed. Cure or careful stabilization can restore what the beast-shape pulls against.
